name: Japan

classification.product_status: Not cells, so outside the Act on the Safety of Regenerative Medicine. Sold with therapeutic claims it becomes a regenerative medicine product or drug under the PMD Act.
classification.clinical_status: Administered as free private medical practice at physician discretion. No committee review, no provision plan, no mandatory adverse-event reporting.
classification.cosmetic_status: Culture supernatant permitted as cosmetic raw material under the Standards for Biological Raw Materials. Human placenta extract prohibited.

legal_basis.instrument: Act on the Safety of Regenerative Medicine
legal_basis.summary: Added in vivo gene therapy. Extracellular vesicles and oligonucleotides explicitly left out of scope.
Governs products. Therapeutic claims require approval.
Governs human-derived cosmetic raw materials. Placenta extract prohibited.

Disease-treatment claims on an unapproved product

recent_actions.note: Proposed bringing EVs into ASRM scope. Not adopted in the 2025 amendment.
Guidance issued to institutions offering supernatant and exosome therapy.

route_in: Fast: supply physicians in the private market, accepting the position rests on a regulatory gap. Durable: an ASRM provision plan or a PMD Act filing with conditional approval.
open_questions: Whether the next amendment cycle brings EVs into scope
Whether personal import at inventory scale draws enforcement

name: South Korea

classification.product_status: Permitted as a cosmetic ingredient with safety standards. No injectable approval exists.
classification.clinical_status: Cell therapies permitted via designated institutions under the 2025 ARBA treatment category. Injecting a cosmetic-grade vial is off-label use of a non-injectable.
classification.cosmetic_status: Permitted with safety standards. The word 'exosome' is banned in advertising unless plant or animal derived.

legal_basis.summary: Created the advanced regenerative medicine treatment category. Designated institutions may treat outside trials and charge patients on five-year approvals. Around 112 institutions designated.
Safety standards for human cell and tissue culture fluid.
Prohibits 'exosome' in cosmetic advertising unless plant or animal derived. Bans hospital-exclusive framing and quantitative anti-ageing claims.

permitted: Manufacturing exosome cosmetics to MFDS standards
Export of cosmetic-grade product
Cell therapy under the ARBA treatment category
Clinical trials under MFDS
grey: Cosmetic-grade vials used intradermally after laser or microneedling
Whether ARBA reaches acellular EVs at all
Products exported as cosmetics and injected in the destination market
prohibited: The word 'exosome' in consumer cosmetic advertising for human-derived product
Medical or drug-like claims on a cosmetic
Intravenous administration of a cosmetic product

recent_actions.note: 237 violations identified, roughly half readable as drug or medical claims.

route_in: A supply market before a sales market. The realistic play is sourcing or co-manufacturing, not selling into it.
open_questions: Whether acellular EVs fall within ARBA scope. Genuinely unresolved.

name: China

classification.product_status: Inside the ATMP framework since June 2025. Exosome-membrane dressings are Class III device combination products since December 2025.
classification.clinical_status: Only within an approved trial or a filed hospital clinical-research study, which cannot charge patients.
classification.cosmetic_status: Prohibited. Human cells, tissues and human-derived products banned as cosmetic ingredients. 'Exosome' not in the approved catalogue.

legal_basis.summary: Brought extracellular vesicles including exosomes into the ATMP framework.
Exosome-membrane dressings defined as Class III combination products.

legal_basis.instrument: Safety and Technical Standards for Cosmetics
legal_basis.summary: Prohibits human-derived cosmetic ingredients. Reaffirmed September 2024 in response to CPPCC Proposal No. 00971.

legal_basis.instrument: Administrative Measures for Stem Cell Clinical Research
legal_basis.summary: Hospital-led research track. Research only, no charging.

permitted: Registered clinical trials under NMPA/CDE
Filed hospital clinical research without charging patients
The Class III device route for qualifying dressings
Manufacturing for export
grey: Plant-derived and conditioned-medium cosmetics avoiding the human-derived ban
Medical-beauty clinics running topical exosome protocols
Human genetic resources rules on cross-border collaboration
prohibited: Any exosome claim or the term on a cosmetic
Injectable human exosomes via medical-beauty and daigou channels
Unregistered cross-border import for clinical use

recent_actions.note: Reaffirmed prohibition on human-derived cosmetic ingredients including exosomes.

route_in: No shortcut. A registered NMPA pathway with a local partner, or stay out. A five-year market, not an entry market.

name: Thailand

classification.product_status: A medicinal product under Thai FDA; an ATMP under the 2026 royal decree. No registration in practice for aesthetic vials.
classification.clinical_status: Only under a registered ATMP or authorised research protocol. Everything else runs on enforcement discretion.
classification.cosmetic_status: Widely used through the aesthetics and wellness channel with no product registration.

legal_basis.instrument: ATMP royal decree and regulatory sandbox
legal_basis.summary: Establishes an ATMP pathway with a sandbox. MOPH roadmap positions Thailand as fastest in ASEAN.

legal_basis.instrument: MOPH standards on stem cell treatment
legal_basis.summary: Outside haematology and corneal/limbal transplants, stem cell treatment is not approved routine care.
GMP laboratory requirements, donor screening for 50+ pathogens, maximum passage number four.
Uses outside recognised standards require a research and ethics framework. Guaranteeing results prohibited.

permitted: A registered ATMP under the new decree
Treatment inside an authorised research protocol with ethics approval
The regulatory sandbox
Licensed facilities operating within scope
grey: Exosomes as an aesthetic and wellness add-on with no product registration
Clinics with facility and physician licences but no product authorisation
'GMP laboratory' claims with no third-party verification

Selling unregistered cell products as routine care

recent_actions.note: Restated that stem cell treatment outside haematology and corneal transplant is not approved routine care.

route_in: The sandbox is the most interesting door in the region. One of few structured routes to a legitimate first commercial footing for an unapproved EV product.
open_questions: Sandbox application criteria and whether a foreign sponsor can apply directly
Whether acellular EVs are in scope of the ATMP decree

name: United Arab Emirates

classification.product_status: No emirate-level exosome standard. Abu Dhabi requires approval from an internationally recognised regulator, which no exosome product holds anywhere.
classification.clinical_status: Clinics are licensed and openly market it. The product has no clean registration route.

legal_basis.instrument: Abu Dhabi DoH Standard on Stem Cell Therapies, Products and Regenerative Medicine
legal_basis.summary: HCT/Ps and stem cell products used in Abu Dhabi must hold product approval from an international regulator recognised by MOHAP.

legal_basis.instrument: DHA Standard on autologous adipose SVF/ADSC therapy
legal_basis.summary: Published standard for autologous adipose procedures. No exosome-specific standard exists.
Governs platelet-rich plasma procedures.

permitted: Operating a licensed clinic with licensed physicians
Autologous adipose SVF and PRP under the DHA standards
Importing a product holding approval from a recognised foreign regulator
grey: Exosome IV drips advertised at 100-200 billion particles
'DHA and MOH approved' language referring to a facility licence, not product approval
Import under a cosmetic, supplement or device classification then clinical administration
prohibited: Marketing a product as approved when only the facility is licensed
Administering an unregistered biologic where recognised foreign approval is required
Disease-treatment claims on a wellness product
route_in: Fastest legitimate footing of any market here: a DoH or DHA-licensed clinic partner, a written protocol, full provenance documentation, honest consent.
open_questions: Whether exosomes fall under semi-controlled medical materials decrees
Whether DHCC free zone rules differ from mainland Dubai

name: Germany (EU baseline)

classification.product_status: Unmodified EVs are not ATMPs per the 2025 EMA/CAT guideline. Handled as biological medicinal products case by case. Engineered EVs carrying functional transgenic mRNA are gene therapy products.
classification.clinical_status: Only with a marketing authorisation or inside an approved trial. The ATMP hospital exemption does not cover naive exosomes.
classification.cosmetic_status: Prohibited. Regulation 1223/2009 bans human cells, tissues and products of human origin. Plant-derived permitted.

legal_basis.summary: Not substantially modified EVs fall outside the ATMP definition. Engineered EVs carrying functional transgenic mRNA classified as gene therapy products.

legal_basis.citation: §13 manufacturing licence, §4b hospital exemption, §20b tissue procurement, §21(2)
legal_basis.summary: §4b hospital exemption applies to ATMPs only, via the Paul-Ehrlich-Institut.
Prohibits human cells, tissues and products of human origin in cosmetics EU-wide.

permitted: Clinical trials under the EU Clinical Trials Regulation via a single CTA
A CAT classification request, free, and the correct first step
Plant-derived exosome cosmetics
Marketing authorisation for a non-ATMP biological
grey: Individueller Heilversuch framing used to justify repeat commercial use
Physician-prepared preparations under narrow §21(2) exemptions
Whether a given engineered product is ATMP or biological
prohibited: Human-derived exosomes in cosmetic products
Importing Korean cosmetic-grade vials for injection
Invoking the ATMP hospital exemption for an unmodified exosome product
Placing an unauthorised medicinal product on the market
route_in: A CAT classification request first. Inexpensive, and it tells you whether you are running a biologics filing or a gene-therapy filing before spending anything.
open_questions: Which national competent authority route is fastest for a non-ATMP biological EV product

name: Switzerland

classification.product_status: Transplant product or medicinal product. Culture expansion is substantial manipulation by definition, so any cultured-cell-derived product is caught.
classification.clinical_status: Not permitted. Cultured-cell products for wellness or aesthetics outside a trial breach Swissmedic rules.
classification.cosmetic_status: Products used in aesthetic medicine to regenerate or repair are treated as transplant products, not cosmetics.

legal_basis.summary: Governs medicinal products including transplant products. Swissmedic ATMP Division is lead regulator.

Transplant products are those manufactured from human or animal tissues or cells by a standardised process, substantially manipulated or used non-homologously. Substantial manipulation includes culture expansion, genetic modification, differentiation or activation.
Governs clinical trials and research involving human subjects.

permitted: Minimally manipulated autologous material for homologous use in a single procedure
Authorised clinical trials
Products holding a Swissmedic marketing authorisation
grey: Where SVF and same-day preparations sit, assessed case by case and sometimes cantonally
Consultation and diagnostics in Switzerland with treatment delivered abroad
prohibited: Expanded or cultured-cell-derived products sold for wellness or aesthetics outside a trial
Importing cosmetic-grade exosome vials for injection
Marketing 'Swiss' regenerative therapy that is neither authorised nor trial-based
Storing UC-MSCs without a Swissmedic licence
route_in: Use Switzerland for credibility, manufacturing partners and capital, not for delivering therapy. There is no permissive Swiss lane.

name: United States (federal)

classification.product_status: Unapproved new drug and unlicensed biological product. Never eligible for the 361 HCT/P exemption. No approval exists for any indication.
classification.clinical_status: Only under an active IND. Nothing else is lawful for a therapeutic purpose.
classification.cosmetic_status: Topical cosmetics permitted with no structure/function claims. Dozens of exosome INCI ingredients exist, mostly plant-derived.

legal_basis.instrument: Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act
legal_basis.summary: Exosome products for therapeutic use are unapproved new drugs.
Unlicensed biological products require a BLA or an active IND.
The 361 exemption requires minimal manipulation and homologous use. The HCT/P definition excludes secreted or extracted human products including cell factors.
FDA warned consumers and providers about unapproved exosome products.

permitted: Topical cosmetics with no structure/function claims
An active IND with a registered clinical trial

name: Florida

classification.product_status: SB 1768 covers stem cell therapy. Its HCT/P definition excludes secreted and extracted human products and cell factors, and requires viable live cells on post-thaw analysis.
classification.clinical_status: The statute does not reach acellular products. A state law cannot authorise what federal law prohibits.
classification.cosmetic_status: Same as US federal. The state law changes only what the medical board may discipline.

legal_basis.summary: Authorises non-FDA-approved stem cell therapy for orthopedics, wound care and pain management, from an FDA-registered facility accredited by NMDP, WMDA, AABB or AATB, with cGMP compliance, disclaimer and consent.
Expressly excludes secreted or extracted human products, such as milk, collagen, and cell factors. Language lifted from 21 CFR 1271.3(d).
Material must contain viable or live cells upon post-thaw analysis, with a lot-specific viability report.

permitted: Stem cell therapy for orthopedics, wound care and pain management meeting all statutory conditions
Topical cosmetics with no structure/function claims

name: Panama

classification.product_status: No product registration category in practical use. Lawfulness sits in the protocol, the facility licence and the consent, not the vial.
classification.clinical_status: Permitted under a MINSA-licensed facility with National Bioethics Committee approval and documented consent.
classification.cosmetic_status: Not the primary channel. Providers typically market secretome or trophic factors rather than exosomes.

legal_basis.summary: MINSA licenses facilities. Cell therapy delivered under approved research and treatment protocols rather than product registration.
Protocols require committee approval. Charging patients within an approved protocol is permitted.

name: Colombia

classification.cosmetic_status: Bundled into IV longevity packages alongside MSCs and hyperbaric oxygen.

legal_basis.summary: Governs handling of tissues and cells. Haematopoietic transplants only at authorised institutions using INVIMA-licensed banks.
Licenses tissue and marrow banks, registers products, supervises trials. Cultured or expanded MSC not approved for routine clinical use.
